entities.summary:
General Motors Company is an American multinational automotive manufacturing company founded in 1908 in Flint, Michigan by William Durant. Once the world's largest automaker for over 70 years, GM's brands including Chevrolet, Cadillac, Buick, and GMC defined American automotive culture and industrial organization for a century.

GM's strategy of offering 'a car for every purse and purpose' — from working-class Chevrolet to wealthy Cadillac — innovated market segmentation that businesses across all industries adopted. Alfred Sloan's management techniques, introduced in the 1920s, created modern divisional corporate organization that became standard management theory globally. GM's dominance peaked in the 1950s when it produced half of all US cars and employed over 600,000 workers.

GM's 2009 bankruptcy — the largest industrial bankruptcy in US history at $173 billion — following the 2008 financial crisis required a $49.5 billion government bailout and reshaped the company by shedding Pontiac, Saturn, Hummer, and Saab brands. The restructured GM focused on Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac, investing heavily in electric vehicles including the Chevy Bolt and Cruise autonomous vehicle division. GM's Lordstown plant transformation from gasoline to electric vehicles symbolizes the broader industrial transition.
